headline: A single real button splits the field by what happens per instance: the hashing lanes re-derive a class every render, the extracted and atomic lanes derive nothing and are then separated by how many bytes their class names cost.

top3.label: StyleX without CSS layers (:not() specificity hack)

microbench.why: `stylex-layers` (0.440 ms/1k) and `next-yak-css-9.7` (0.478) put nothing on the render path at all, and both beat hand-written `vanilla` at 0.489 because their emitted markup is shorter than the hand-written class list. The cost of the losers is one function each: `emotion` at 2.85 ms/1k spends 100 ms of a 219 ms JS window inside `@emotion/hash`, re-hashing the serialized rule set per instance, and `styled-components` at 2.00 spends 130 ms of 178 inside its own package doing the same through `generateAndInjectStyles`. `bamboo` (1.10) and `panda` (1.34) again pay in react-dom rather than in styling, 79.0 and 99.8 ms of it.

autocannon.why: The ranking flips against the microbench and payload is why: `next-yak-9.7` serves 596 req/s on 4.93 kB while `stylex-layers`, which renders faster, serves 413 on 9.10 kB. Below that the per-request work takes over, `styled-components` (173) and `emotion` (128) re-hashing a thousand buttons on every request, and `panda-props` (80) resolving a style prop per element.

attribution.why: `next-yak-9.7` folds the button into a plain `<button className>` and keeps a 0.291 ms library slice; `stylex-layers` and `vanilla` report no library time at all and pay 0.330 and 0.310 ms of component self-time reading their static class constants. The whole spread above that is per-instance derivation: `emotion` 5.35 ms of library plus 0.634 of component, `styled-components` 4.55, `goober` 4.32 with 123 ms inside its own package, `tailwind-merge` 1.69 ms re-running the merge. `bamboo` and `panda` are the odd pair, zero library time and 3.18 and 3.92 ms total, all of it react-dom writing 9.16 and 11.5 kB of class attributes.

hydrate.why: The button hydrates as pure JS in every lane whose sheet is a file: 61.5-64.1 ms for `bamboo`, both 9.7 lanes, `stylex` and `vanilla`, with zero style and zero layout inside the span. `styled-components` and `goober` both reach 169 ms because they inject during hydration and their spans show 0.575 and 0.466 ms of recalculation plus a layout pass; `emotion` at 124 ms re-serializes without the layout.

inp.why: Pressing the button re-renders one element, and every lane that decided its class at build time does it in under 1 ms of span JS, clustering at 6.7-7.7 ms. The hashing lanes re-derive the class on the interaction instead, `emotion` reaching 31.5 ms and `goober` 22.7; `panda-props` at 27.0 ms re-resolves its style props for a single button.

mount.why: Cold mount is dominated by the one sheet parse, so the extracted, atomic and hand-written lanes all land at 116-121 ms. `emotion` (191 ms), `styled-components` (172) and `goober` (171) build their sheet before the first paint, and `emotion`'s 8.89 ms layout against `vanilla`'s 5.75 shows the browser waiting on it.

top3.label: StyleX without CSS layers (:not() specificity hack)

renderTiming.why: One recalculation, one layout and two paints in every lane, so the counts tie completely. Only recalc cost separates them, 0.361-0.442 ms for the lanes with a static sheet against `emotion`'s 0.540 and `styled-components`' 0.502, and even that gap is a single measurement.

payload.why: The css-prop fold ships 3.95 kB gzipped with zero styling JS, below `vanilla`'s 4.44 kB, because the button's pseudo-states and media query collapse into one numbered class. The runtime lanes carry their compiler: `emotion` 12.9 kB of JS inside 16.9 total, `styled-components` 13.4 inside 17.4. The atomic lanes pay in markup instead, `bamboo` 9.16 kB of HTML inside 12.1 kB and `panda` 11.5 inside 17.3.

nsweep.why: Everything that decided its classes at build time is linear and indistinguishable at 4,000 buttons: 4.77-4.99 ms across `stylex-layers`, `vanilla`, `next-yak-css-9.7`, `next-yak-9.7` and `stylex`. The hashing lanes multiply their per-instance function by n, `emotion` reaching 29.3 ms and `styled-components` 20.6, and `panda-props` 39.3 ms is the steepest line in the case.
